clue.text: Quiet walks to a scene of carnage

blocks.note: sh! is the call for quiet
to amble is to walk at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: A quiet stroll leads someone straight into the aftermath of a massacre.
explanation.walkthrough: A shambles was originally a meat market or slaughterhouse, hence a place of bloodshed; the everyday sense of a mess came later.
explanation.definitionFit: The old meaning of the word is a slaughterhouse or butchers' street, so any bloody place of slaughter.

clue.text: Lead the others in poll support

explanation.walkthrough: 'poll' looks like an election; it is the old word for the head, as in a poll tax charged per head.
explanation.definitionFit: Poll is an old word for the head, and this cushion on a car seat supports the head.

clue.text: Friends found here in restaurant, say, after start of meal

blocks.note: the first letter of meal
an eating house is an old name for a restaurant

explanation.surface: Friends meet up at a restaurant once the meal has started.
explanation.walkthrough: Friends with a capital F are Quakers, members of the Religious Society of Friends; M plus the restaurant word, spoken, gives their place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Quakers call themselves the Society of Friends and worship in a building known by this name.

clue.text: Food in the States swallowed by wise guy

clue.text: Tramp's ferret gets duck

explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is an American word for a homeless wanderer, the same as a vagrant or tramp.

clue.text: Table of belief

second meaning: trust or acceptance that something is true

clue.text: A knock about comedy is 1

definitions.note: a cross-reference: the answer to 1 across, a place of slaughter

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for comedy is read back to front

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone declares that a bit of slapstick knockabout comedy is a complete shambles.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 points to 1 across, SHAMBLES, in its old sense of a slaughterhouse; 'knockabout' reads as one word but splits into knock and about.
explanation.definitionFit: A shambles in its original sense was a slaughterhouse, which is exactly what an abattoir is.

clue.text: Watch out for the hole

explanation.walkthrough: Cave (said KAY-vee) is the Latin imperative 'beware', once shouted at British public schools when a master approached.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin warning call and the natural hollow in rock are spelt the same, giving two unrelated senses.

clue.text: In 3. you start to speak and fail many times over

clue.text: Unfeigned anger at kings' gift

clue.text: You won't win a game here until you're past forty
